source.title: Maladaptive striatal plasticity and abnormal reward-learning in cervical dystonia.

confidence_rationale: Fits a basal-ganglia model with explicit, separable D1:LTP/LTD and D2:LTP/LTD corticostriatal learning rules to human reversal-learning behaviour and finds that a specific asymmetry (decreased D2:LTP/LTD) best explains a clinical phenotype, with learning rates tracking symptom severity. This is direct empirical support that the D1-LTP/D2-LTD asymmetry ARC-108 names is a real, load-bearing, individually-varying parameter and that its derangement maps to a disorder -- exactly ARC-108's psychiatric_failure_mode requirement. Down-weighted because the phenotype is a movement disorder (dystonia), not the dopaminergic-RPE psychopathologies ARC-108 names (addiction/schizophrenia/anhedonia), so the failure-mode mapping is by analogy of mechanism, not of syndrome.
failure_signatures: If REE collapses D1 and D2 plasticity into a single symmetric learning rule, it forfeits the degree of freedom that here distinguishes patients from controls -- the model could not have separated reward-phase from loss-phase deficits without independent D1 and D2 LTP/LTD terms.

Excessive D2 corticostriatal depotentiation selectively impaired the post-reversal (relearning) phase; a gating substrate with a deranged D2-LTD branch would show intact initial acquisition but pathological inflexibility -- a concrete failure signature to watch for in the E3 selector.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Fitting a basal-ganglia model with receptor-specific corticostriatal learning rules (D1:LTP/LTD and D2:LTP/LTD, each up or down) to a reward gain / loss-avoidance reversal task, a model with decreased D2:LTP/LTD best explained cervical dystonia patients' selective post-reversal impairment, and individual reward-reversal learning rates correlated with motor symptom severity.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct support for the D1-LTP / D2-LTD asymmetry that ARC-108 builds into its learned gating rule: the two receptor branches are separable, individually parameterised, and their imbalance is behaviourally consequential and clinically graded -- which is precisely why ARC-108 wants them as distinct learnable terms rather than one symmetric weight update.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The clinical phenotype is cervical dystonia (a movement disorder), not the dopaminergic-RPE psychopathologies ARC-108 explicitly names. The mechanistic mapping (separable D1/D2 LTP-LTD branches whose asymmetry matters) is strong; the syndrome-level mapping to ARC-108's psychiatric_failure_mode list is by analogy, not direct.
mapping.source_context: Human patients (40 cervical dystonia, 40 controls) performing a reward/loss-avoidance reversal task, behaviour fitted to a computational basal-ganglia model.

confidence_components.notes: Human behaviour + model fit is solid empirical grounding; transfer_risk elevated because the syndrome (dystonia) is off-target relative to ARC-108's named failure modes.
